title: Reduce Completed pilot evidence packet export
summary: Removed the transitional Completed pilot evidence packet flat export while preserving mediaPipelineCompletedView.renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket(). Pending Publish and Command History now render the packet through the Completed namespace helper, backend-served/browser tests guard against flat-assignment regression, and generated WebView inventory/contract artifacts report 501 flat exports.
reason: Continue namespace-first WebView cleanup in the touched Completed/Pending proof domain without changing backend ownership, media policy, pending-publish drain, filesystem mutation, or source media handling.
behavior_before: completedView.js exposed renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket through mediaPipelineCompletedView and as a transitional window.renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket flat export. Pending Publish and Command History still read the flat alias.
behavior_after: renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket remains available through mediaPipelineCompletedView only. Pending Publish and Command History use the namespace helper, the Completed/Pending browser smoke fails if the served flat assignment returns, and the documented flat-export count is 501 across 49 files.
tests_added: Extended tests/webview/test_webview_browser_completed_pending_proof_smoke.py to reject a served window.renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket flat assignment.
Updated tests/python/desktop/test_application_facade_local_api.py to require the namespace export and reject window.renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket.
rollback_plan: Restore the window.renderCompletedPilotEvidencePacket assignment in completedView.js, move the touched consumers back to the flat alias only if compatibility is intentionally required, regenerate the WebView public contract baseline and summaries, and rerun the same WebView/static validation ladder.
notes:
Source-media safety: this is a frontend compatibility-export cleanup only. It does not change backend routes, strict confirmations, repair/apply behavior, pending-publish manifests, drain behavior, filesystem mutation, source/scratch/output handling, FFmpeg arguments, or media policy. No downloads or real-media validation are required for this low-risk WebView namespace cleanup.
